ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Ludwig van Beethoven

text.paragraph: Mr. van Beethoven returns six months after his first visit, four weeks after the blocked left ear was cleared. His hearing feels as it did in the summer. He wears the aids all day, and the left aid has not whistled since the dome was replaced. The tinnitus is quieter in his mind and he sleeps through most nights. He has finished his planned therapy sessions and will keep monthly sessions through the winter. He has started an introductory American Sign Language class with a friend and says it has been a pleasure to meet Deaf people who do not treat hearing as the measure of a life. His HIV test from the preventive visit was nonreactive. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-19; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Weber lateralizes to the right; Rinne positive on both sides

Progressive hearing loss in both ears over about three years, worse on the left, with poor understanding of soft speech; type and cause not yet established at intake; audiology and otolaryngology evaluation requested
S — Synthetic presenting concern anchored to his documented account; superseded by the diagnosis at the audiologic evaluation.

Persistent, bothersome tinnitus in both ears for about three years, constant ringing and buzzing day and night, with intolerance of loud sound; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented tinnitus
S — Synthetic modern coding of the documented tinnitus.
Adjustment disorder with depressed mood in response to progressive hearing loss, with withdrawal from social gatherings; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented despair and isolation
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the documented letters describe distress and withdrawal, and the record makes no claim about his real mental health.

Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss, asymmetric (left worse than right), sloping from normal or mild in the low frequencies to moderately severe in the high frequencies; no air-bone gap; synthetic modern episode linked to his documented progressive deafness, whose cause remains unknown
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the audiologic evaluation; it states no cause, because the retrospective theories are disputed.
Impacted cerumen, left ear, in a hearing aid user, causing a sudden muffling of hearing on that side; removed by irrigation with hearing restored; resolved
S — Synthetic acute problem; not a historical claim.

list.item:
Bilateral sensorineural hearing loss with hearing aids (H90.3). Repeat audiogram: right ear unchanged; left ear unchanged through 3000 Hz and 5 dB worse at 4000 and 8000 Hz (75 and 80 dB HL), within test-retest variation; four-frequency averages 35 (right) and 50 (left) dB HL. Word recognition 88% on the right and 60% on the left, from 64%. Stable for now, but the loss has been progressive, and the plan is to keep testing. [S]
Audiogram yearly and with any change; otolaryngology review in one year.
Ear canals checked at each visit.

Persistent, bothersome tinnitus, bilateral (H93.13). Tinnitus Handicap Inventory 28, from 58; the six-month goal is met. [S]
Continue sound enrichment as needed.

Adjustment disorder with depressed mood (F43.21). PHQ-9 4, in remission; GAD-7 4. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or self-harm. [S]
Monthly therapy through the winter.
PHQ-9 every three months for the next year, sooner if his hearing changes.

tr.td: Targeted ear examination: otoscopy, tuning forks, cranial nerves
Canals clear; tuning forks at baseline
Comprehensive audiologic evaluation: pure-tone air and bone conduction, speech audiometry with word recognition, tympanometry, acoustic reflexes
Promptly for tinnitus with hearing difficulty; repeat at six months while progressive, then yearly and with any change
Left 4000 and 8000 Hz 5 dB worse, within test-retest variation; word recognition 88% and 60%
MRI of the internal auditory canals with gadolinium
When the loss or tinnitus is asymmetric or unilateral, or with focal neurologic signs
Normal five months ago; repeat only if the asymmetry grows or new signs appear
Tinnitus impact (Tinnitus Handicap Inventory, recorded in the note; no LOINC code is used)
At the start of management and when treatment changes
Cognitive behavioral therapy for persistent, bothersome tinnitus and the adjustment disorder
Planned course finished; monthly sessions continue
Hearing aid evaluation, fitting with real-ear verification, and use (data logging)
Evaluation when persistent tinnitus comes with documented hearing loss; review use at each visit after fitting
All-day use; left dome replaced after the impaction
At the start; reinforce at each visit
At diagnosis and after any episode
Reviewed after last month's blocked ear: same-day visit for sudden loss without a blocked canal
Started an ASL class by his own choice; accommodations working
At baseline and at least monthly during active treatment; every 2 to 4 weeks in continuation
Depression measure (PHQ-9), monthly during active treatment
At least monthly during active treatment

Protocol deviation: no PHQ-9 in the six weeks between the three-month visit and the preventive visit. No harm resulted: the next PHQ-9 was 5 and today's is 4. Corrective action: a nurse care manager phone PHQ-9 between visits whenever visits are more than four weeks apart during active treatment
At baseline and with PHQ-9 reviews
Suicide-risk review (PHQ-9 item 9 and structured questions since the last visit), safety plan, and the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
No thoughts of suicide or self-harm

list.item: Bilateral hearing aids fitted, verified, and worn at least eight hours a day by three months. Outcome by 2026-07-13: Fitted at five weeks with real-ear verification; data logging showed about eleven hours a day at three months [S]

Tinnitus no longer the main barrier to work and sleep, with the Tinnitus Handicap Inventory at least 20 points lower by six months. Outcome by 2026-10-19: Tinnitus Handicap Inventory 28, from 58; sleeping through most nights [S]
PHQ-9 below 5 by six months. Outcome by 2026-10-19: PHQ-9 4 [S]

Communication access he chooses in place for rehearsals, teaching, and meetings by three months. Outcome by 2026-07-13: Remote microphone for teaching and rehearsals, live speech-to-text on his phone, and written agendas; he chose to tell his closest colleagues [S]
Hearing protection for loud rehearsals by five weeks. Outcome by 2026-05-18: Custom musicians' earplugs with flat attenuation fitted with the hearing aids [S]
